newsitem.title: UK: No talk of OPEC output rise to cash in on higher prices.
newsitem.headline: No talk of OPEC output rise to cash in on higher prices.

text.p: The Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries is not rushing to cash in on the unexpected oil price bonanza by increasing its oil output, Gulf oil and OPEC sources said Tuesday.

The sources, representing several OPEC members, said it was too early to talk about the oil cartel boosting its 25 million barrel a day production ceiling to take advantage of the increased demand for its oil. OPEC production is running about 800,000 barrels a day above its ceiling.
"There have been no discussion at all on this matter. It is too early to say what we will do in November," a Gulf source familar with Saudi policy said
Some delegates said OPEC powerhouse Saudi Arabia and other large producers were not keen to open up debate on how to divide any increases among the 11 members of the group.

"The price simply is not high enough for us to rush to increase the ceiling. We would be opening Pandora's box by raising it. Everyone would be demanding more quota than they could produce," said an OPEC delegate.

On Tuesday, October crude oil was off 14 cents at $23.05 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange after jumping last week to $25.35 -- near its post-Gulf war high of $25.70 a barrel set April 16 -- on jitters about U.S.-Iraqi tensions.
A U.N. agreement to allow Iraq to resume oil sales has been put on hold following the military confrontation between Iraq and the United States.
The delay in Iraqi oil sales, strong demand and unexpected supply cuts from non-OPEC producers in the North Sea and Latin America have lifted prices well above analysts' predictions.
Prices are about $6 above year-ago levels adding unexpected millions to the coffers of oil producing countries.

OPEC ministers next meet on Nov. 27 in Vienna and will discuss production levels for at least the first six months of 1997. A Gulf source familar with Saudi oil policy said the kingdom expected oil prices to stay strong until the end of the year.
